title: AI agents in customer service: Benefits and use cases | Pylon
summary: See how AI agents in customer service resolve tickets, work across Slack and Teams, and free up your team for complex work. Then, explore Pylon's approach.
body_markdown:
Today’s AI agents have moved beyond basic chatbots and ticket deflection to autonomously complete multi-step tasks, answer customers’ questions across multiple channels, and route requests to the right team.


In this guide, we’ll explore what else AI agents in customer service can do, their benefits for B2B support teams, and how to make the most of them.


## What’s an AI customer service agent?


Ask AI view from Pylon


An AI customer service agent is software that can natively understand customer requests and take actions with limited human involvement. In customer service, AI agents and chatbots work differently: Chatbots can answer simple questions with pre-scripted logic. Agents can support and augment your team to pull account context, autonomously complete simple tasks for customers, or investigate questions on your teams’ behalf.


Let’s say a customer sees an error message in your B2B SaaS platform whenever they try to export data from the analytics dashboard. A traditional chatbot could suggest general solutions based on scripted answers before escalating to a support team member, but an AI agent could:


- **Interpret intent.** The AI agent analyzes the message to understand exactly what the customer needs.
- **Retrieve relevant context.** The agent searches account context to see if the customer has had data export issues before and looks for relevant details from the knowledge base and other customer conversations about the same problem.
- **Determine the next action.** Instead of simply providing information, the AI agent uses context to attempt a resolution. In this case, it might discover that the customer’s database is unusually large and determine that the best next step is to export part of the dataset instead of everything at once.
- **Respond or complete a task.** The AI agent tells the customer about the suggested fix and, if appropriate, tries to export the smaller section of data itself.
- **Escalate when human judgment is needed.** If the AI agent can’t fix the problem, it escalates the issue to the customer support team and includes a full explanation of the issue and the fixes it has already tried.


With the help of AI agents, B2B support teams can offload significant amounts of labor to better focus on complex tickets without sacrificing customer relationships.


## What are AI agents used for in customer service?


Here are the most common ways you’ll see an AI agent used for customer support:


- **Answers questions.** AI agents can save time for your team and your customers by giving instant answers to common questions. They give more accurate answers than chatbots because they can access context like support tickets, account data, and knowledge-base content without needing manual script updates.
- **Investigates issues.** Your team can use AI agents to investigate customer issues and suggest solutions to save time on research and increase[time to resolution](https://www.usepylon.com/blog/time-to-resolution) .
- **Routes and prioritizes requests.** Automated routing also speeds up response times. AI agents can prioritize and route issues more accurately when they analyze messages to identify customer sentiment and intent. They can also draw on account context to identify high-priority customers or urgent issues and address them accordingly.
- **Troubleshoots product issues.** AI agents are better at troubleshooting than a traditional chatbot because they can check logs and status pages, search recent incidents, and check the customer’s past conversations to find likely fixes and resolve issues autonomously.
- **Updates customer or account information.** When you give AI agents access to your operational systems, they can take actions like adding or removing users on a customer’s account and updating plan details, and escalate when human approval is required.
- **Handles billing issues.** When you connect an AI agent to your billing systems,they can also resolve billing problems, update order statuses, and manage subscriptions.
- **Summarizes conversations.** B2B customer support often involves long conversation threads with multiple stakeholders. AI agents save time and summarize those responses to give your team the context they need to resolve issues.


## Benefits of AI agents for customer service teams


AI agents are already creating measurable improvements in operational efficiency and[customer experience metrics](https://www.usepylon.com/blog/ai-customer-experience) for B2B support teams.


Response and resolution times are one of the biggest metrics that AI agents can support. Because they can give instant answers to repetitive, high-volume requests, AI agents can[reduce ticket volume](https://www.usepylon.com/blog/ai-ticket-deflection-reduce-support-volume-2025) and help teams to clear backlogs in the ticket queue for faster responses to new tickets.


AI agents give your team access to more context and help them research queries more quickly. They can act as a copilot that summarizes issues and drafts responses, which frees up even more of your support team’s time for future tickets.


AI agents also open 24/7 coverage for customers in different time zones or who work without hiring more team members to cover night shifts and weekends.


The customer experience improves with AI agents because customers receive faster answers, more consistent service, and fewer unnecessary handoffs. Faster, more accurate responses create a[better customer experience](https://www.usepylon.com/blog/ai-for-customer-experience) , which you can track through metrics like[customer satisfaction score (CSAT)](https://www.usepylon.com/blog/customer-satisfaction-score) and customer effort score (CES).


## How AI agents work across customer service channels


Triggers view from Pylon


AI agents don’t only work in a chat interface. When they’re part of an[omnichannel support platform](https://www.usepylon.com/blog/omnichannel-customer-support-definition-examples-strategy) , they can handle customer requests across every channel your team members and customers interact, like chat, email, and platforms like Slack and Microsoft Teams.


In B2B support, it’s common to see stakeholders from the same account ask questions on different channels. When you implement AI agents in customer service, integrate them with your customer relationship management (CRM) system so that they connect tickets across different channels and pull in all the relevant account context.


Using the SaaS dashboard example we looked at earlier, the customer’s data analyst might send a Slack message, and an executive might follow up with an email about the same issue. When you connect your AI agent to their account context, it can treat those issues as a single request instead of processing them as separate tickets. Your team avoids duplicate work, and customers don’t have to repeat themselves.


Some[AI-powered customer support platforms](https://www.usepylon.com/blog/ai-powered-customer-support-guide) also include AI agents that work in Slack and Teams, without needing a channel switch. Pylon’s[Slack Agent](https://www.usepylon.com/ai-agents/slack) gives every team self-service access to Pylon information by tagging @Pylon, for example, so teams can get instant answers and take action without ever leaving Slack. Other agents in Pylon can investigate customer issues and resolve simple ones on its own in the channels you deploy it to.


Although AI agents can resolve many issues automatically, complex or sensitive tasks still need human judgement. Choose a tool that allows[human teams and AI agents to work together](https://www.usepylon.com/blog/ai-agents-customer-support-teams) instead of aiming for full automation.

## FAQ


### Is AI taking over customer support?


AI platforms are automating a growing share of support work, but human agents are still critical for B2B teams. They can handle more complex tickets and manage multi-stakeholder enterprise relationships with empathy. The future of AI in customer support is more likely to look like a team effort between traditional team members and AI agents.


### What are the best AI customer support platforms?


There are many examples of AI agents in customer service to choose from, and the best platform depends on your team’s needs. Consider their automation needs and how an AI agent (or multiple) would fit into the channels and workflows they already use. Growing B2B customer support teams with strong enterprise relationships and complex ticket needs will likely find success with Pylon, but other common options include Fin, Zendesk AI, and Salesforce Agentforce.


### How accurate are AI customer service agents?


It depends on the accuracy of the AI agent’s source data and accessible information. Test and monitor the system regularly to get reliable responses, and make sure that knowledge bases and internal data are updated whenever there’s a process change.


### Is customer data safe when using AI agents?


The average security depends on the platform and how you implement an agent. Check the data privacy and access control procedures of your chosen platform before deployment, and set up guardrails to limit how the AI agent can access and use sensitive customer data.


### How long does it take to implement an AI customer service agent?


Some AI agents come ready to use immediately after installation, while others can take weeks to onboard. Implementation time varies based on complexity and scope of the initial deployment, including necessary integrations, knowledge-base readiness, and testing requirements.
